Differentially private scree values

Source: R/scree.R
dp_scree.Rd

Estimates scree values along private principal component directions using means of squared differences from disjoint score pairs. An ordinary PCA reference is computed only when non_private = TRUE.

Usage

dp_scree(
  X,
  k,
  privacy,
  method = c("clipped", "pmwm", "huber"),
  control = NULL,
  cpp.option = TRUE,
  mono = TRUE,
  V_dp = NULL,
  non_private = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'dp_scree'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'dp_scree'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.dp_scree'
print(x, digits = 4, ...)

Arguments

X

A numeric matrix or data frame with observations in rows and variables in columns. Non-numeric data-frame columns are excluded with a warning; numeric values must be finite. At least two observations and one numeric feature are required. If directions must be estimated, the pairwise-separation condition of dp_loading() also applies.

k

Number of leading components to estimate; an integer from 1 to the number of retained numeric features.

privacy

A privacy_control() object allocating budget to loading and scree (equal shares by default). Each requested scree method receives the full scree allocation.

method

One or more scree estimators: "clipped", "pmwm", or "huber" ("clipped" by default).

control

Tuning parameters from clipped_control(), pmwm_control(), or huber_control(). For multiple methods, supply a named list of method-specific controls; required tuning values must be supplied.

cpp.option

Whether to use the compiled spherical-Kendall implementation (TRUE by default) when estimating private directions; ignored if V_dp is supplied.

mono

Whether to apply nonincreasing isotonic regression (TRUE by default). Negative scree estimates are truncated to zero in either case.

V_dp

Optional p by p private PC direction matrix (NULL by default), where p is the number of numeric PCA features. Columns must be orthonormal and rows must follow the feature order in X; matching row names are required when both sets of names exist.

non_private

Whether to compute and store ordinary PCA reference results (FALSE by default). The reference contains ordinary PCA scree and PVE.

x

A summary.dp_scree object.

...

Further arguments, reserved for compatibility with the generic.

object

A dp_scree object.

digits

Number of significant digits used for printing.

Value

A dp_scree list containing one entry per requested method (clipped, pmwm, and/or huber). Each entry has scree and pve vectors named PC1, ..., PCk. The nonprivate entry holds the optional ordinary PCA reference (or NULL when omitted), and metadata stores input dimensions, methods and the recorded privacy budget. PVE is normalized over the k returned components in every entry. Use summary() for scree, PVE and cumulative PVE tables, and plot() to draw stored estimates without a new randomized computation.

Invisibly returns x.

A summary.dp_scree object containing one table per stored method. Each table gives scree values, PVE and cumulative PVE. PVE is normalized over the fitted components, as in dp_scree(). Printing the summary shows component importance by method and the privacy allocations.

Details

Let Y = X V be scores along the private directions. For each method, m = floor(n / 2) disjoint pairs of rows are formed and the component-wise values are $$W_{jl} = (Y_{b_j,l} - Y_{a_j,l})^2/2.$$ An odd final observation is unused. The methods privately estimate the column means of W, corresponding to variance along private directions rather than necessarily to sample covariance eigenvalues.

The estimators differ as follows:

  • "clipped": Clip the paired values at C_clip, then perturb their mean vector with Gaussian noise.

  • "pmwm": Estimate private lower and upper quantiles, winsorize the paired values, and perturb their mean vector with Gaussian noise. Quantile calls share half of the method's epsilon; the mean receives the remaining half and all delta.

  • "huber": Estimate private component scales and apply noisy Huber gradient updates. The scale step uses m2_frac of epsilon; the updates use the remainder and all delta. At least eight observations are required.

Directions are estimated once unless V_dp is supplied. The input is not automatically centered or standardized; sensitivity arguments use fixed-size replacement adjacency and condition on the directions. Data-dependent scaling requires separate privacy analysis. Sample size, schema, component selection, and tuning parameters are assumed public.

Each requested scree method uses the full scree allocation. Releasing several methods together, or releasing results from repeated calls, requires composition beyond the stored budget for a single method. The optional ordinary PCA reference is not private.

Scree values are truncated at zero, optionally made nonincreasing, and normalized over the returned k components for PVE. A zero total yields zero PVE. These steps are post-processing and do not reorder the directions.

References

Dwork C, Roth A (2014). “The Algorithmic Foundations of Differential Privacy.” Found. Trends Theor. Comput. Sci., 9(3–4), 211–407. ISSN 1551-305X, doi:10.1561/0400000042 .

Ramsay K, Spicker D (2025). “Improved subsample-and-aggregate via the private modified winsorized mean.” Code available at https://github.com/12ramsake/PMWM, 2501.14095, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14095.

Durfee D (2023). “Unbounded Differentially Private Quantile and Maximum Estimation.” In Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 36, 77691–77712. doi:10.52202/075280-3394 , https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/hash/f4b6ef2a78684dca2fb3f1c09372e041-Abstract-Conference.html.

Yu M, Ren Z, Zhou W (2024). “Gaussian differentially private robust mean estimation and inference.” Bernoulli, 30(4), 3059–3088.

Kim M, Jung S (2025). “Robust and Differentially Private Principal Component Analysis.” Statistical Analysis and Data Mining: An ASA Data Science Journal, 18(6), e70053. doi:10.1002/sam.70053 .

See also

dp_loading() for private principal component direction estimation. clipped_control(), pmwm_control(), and huber_control() for method-specific tuning parameters.

Examples

data(gau, package = "dppca")

# Use a small subset to keep the example fast.
X <- gau[1:100, ]
privacy <- privacy_control(eps = 3, delta = 1e-4)

# Estimate clipped private scree values and an ordinary PCA comparison.
set.seed(123)
out <- dp_scree(
  X,
  k = 2,
  privacy = privacy,
  method = "clipped",
  control = clipped_control(C_clip = 3)
)

out$nonprivate
#> NULL
out$clipped
#> $scree
#>       PC1       PC2 
#> 0.7621344 0.7621344 
#> 
#> $pve
#> PC1 PC2 
#> 0.5 0.5 
#> 

# Multiple methods can be requested together by using a named control list.
# Loading is estimated once; each method receives the full scree budget.
# Change the split in privacy_control() to choose a different allocation.
